subcomponents.title: Uses scene-kit APIs without bypassing or duplicating them

criteria.rationale: Talk passes its steps to the reusable Presentation host. The shared Scene composes scene-kit nodes, whose implementations provide Motion layout IDs; Stage supplies the shared scene mount.
evidence: Talk renders Presentation with STEPS.
Scene uses SceneLayer, Box, Label, Arrow, Frame, Emphasis, and SymbolChip; the node implementations assign layoutId from each supplied id.

subcomponents.title: Uses stable identities and appropriate grouped-scene architecture

criteria.rationale: The nine steps are generated from the titles array, and each uses the same Scene and groupKey. Talk passes those steps to Presentation, which passes the active step to Stage. Stage uses groupKey and Scene name for the keyed scene wrapper, keeping that wrapper’s key stable across steps. Separately, Scene passes presentation-owned ENTITY values as node IDs; the scene-kit exports resolve those nodes to primitives that assign each ID to motion layoutId.
evidence: STEPS maps all nine titles to steps with Scene, a beat payload, and groupKey 'how-to-evolving-scene'.
Stage forms sceneKey from groupKey and Scene name and uses it as the keyed motion scene wrapper.
Scene reuses ENTITY IDs across beats; the exported Box, Label, Arrow, Frame, Emphasis, and SymbolChip primitives set layoutId={id}.

demo-integration.rationale: Talk passes its steps to the reusable Presentation host. The shared Scene composes scene-kit nodes, whose implementations provide Motion layout IDs; Stage supplies the shared scene mount.
evidence: Talk renders Presentation with STEPS.
Scene uses SceneLayer, Box, Label, Arrow, Frame, Emphasis, and SymbolChip; the node implementations assign layoutId from each supplied id.

demo-integration.rationale: The nine steps are generated from the titles array, and each uses the same Scene and groupKey. Talk passes those steps to Presentation, which passes the active step to Stage. Stage uses groupKey and Scene name for the keyed scene wrapper, keeping that wrapper’s key stable across steps. Separately, Scene passes presentation-owned ENTITY values as node IDs; the scene-kit exports resolve those nodes to primitives that assign each ID to motion layoutId.
evidence: STEPS maps all nine titles to steps with Scene, a beat payload, and groupKey 'how-to-evolving-scene'.
Stage forms sceneKey from groupKey and Scene name and uses it as the keyed motion scene wrapper.
Scene reuses ENTITY IDs across beats; the exported Box, Label, Arrow, Frame, Emphasis, and SymbolChip primitives set layoutId={id}.

demo-integration.rationale: The required presentation title is passed through and rendered, but the public PresentationProps contract also accepts children that Presentation never reads or renders. That is a dead public input.
evidence: Talk supplies title; Presentation forwards it to Header, which renders it in browse mode.
PresentationProps declares children, while Presentation destructures and renders the other inputs without consuming children.

demo-integration.rationale: Progress and section controls expose semantic current state and stable active-state attributes, with presentation-local CSS targeting the active controls. The Footer implements the default attribution link locally, and the presentation styles its hook locally.
evidence: Footer sets aria-current and data-presentation-active on progress buttons; Toc does the same for section buttons.
Footer renders the default 'made by and-scene' GitHub link with a presentation-attribution hook; the presentation stylesheet styles that hook.

demo-integration.rationale: The registry points to the demo's Talk. Its step data, entity IDs, Scene, and styling live in the presentation folder. Talk delegates hosting to the shared Presentation boundary, which handles navigation, chrome, and Stage without demo-specific branches.
evidence: The registry loads the demo Talk, which imports local STEPS and CSS.
The local STEPS, ENTITY values, Scene, and stylesheet contain the demo implementation; Presentation handles the active step through reusable components.

scene-kit.rationale: Each active step supplies its own identity, title, caption, and scene payload. Presentation selects the step by index and passes its metadata and payload to the rendered components.
evidence: STEPS creates distinct ids, titles, captions, and beat payloads; Presentation passes the selected step to Header, Stage, and Footer.

scene-kit.rationale: The visible step number comes from the active array index, so reordering steps changes their displayed numbers without editing step data.
evidence: Header renders String(index + 1).padStart(2, '0'); Presentation supplies nav.index.

scene-kit.rationale: The authored steps use a beat payload, and Stage passes that payload to the scene component, where it controls rendered entities.
evidence: STEPS is Step<Payload>[]; Stage renders <Scene payload={step.payload} />; Scene reads payload.beat.

scene-kit.rationale: Stable entity IDs feed Motion layout identity inside a LayoutGroup, providing a persisting layout animation path across step updates.
evidence: Box and other node primitives render motion elements with layout and layoutId={id}; Stage keeps grouped scenes under LayoutGroup, and the sample reuses entity IDs.

scene-kit.rationale: The continuing layout motion does not consume a shared settlement duration or completion signal. The Appear delay is a separate fixed value, and ordinary new sample entities are conditionally rendered without Appear.
evidence: Node primitives set layout and layoutId without a transition using LAYOUT_T; Appear defaults to ENTER_DELAY; Scene conditionally adds entities as beat increases.

scene-kit.rationale: The scene boundary animates removal of an entire keyed scene, but it does not preserve ordinarily conditionally removed entities for exit. The sample's conditional entities have no entity exit path.
evidence: AnimatePresence wraps the scene div in Stage; Scene conditionally renders individual nodes; the node primitives provide no exit handling.

scene-kit.rationale: Steps sharing a group and Scene component retain the same scene key while their payload changes, allowing the mounted scene to update in place.
evidence: Stage derives sceneKey from groupKey and Scene identity; all sample steps use the same groupKey and Scene; the focused test asserts the scene element remains the same after navigation and its content…

scene-kit.rationale: Grouped updates keep the scene mounted, and continuing child nodes remain in the same conditional branches with stable IDs rather than remounting through newcomer entry state.
evidence: Stage retains the same keyed scene for grouped steps; Scene renders the you node at every beat and retains previously introduced nodes at later beats; ordinary nodes have no initial newcomer animatio…

scene-kit.rationale: The grouped sample uses one scene whose beat conditions add and retain deliberately placed entities across the sequence.
evidence: Every step points to the same Scene and groupKey; SceneLayer contains position-assigned nodes that accumulate through beat conditions.

scene-kit.rationale: Present mode shows the active title and stage while omitting browse footer and table of contents.
evidence: Presentation renders the present title instead of Footer when mode is present and only renders Toc in browse mode; the focused test checks caption removal after switching.

scene-kit.rationale: Browse mode renders the active title and caption, section table of contents, previous and next controls, and progress buttons. The authored wide-viewport CSS shows the table of contents.
evidence: Presentation renders Toc and Footer in browse mode; Footer renders h1, caption paragraph, controls, and progress; sample CSS displays the Toc except at its narrow breakpoint.

scene-kit.rationale: Toggling mode changes only mode state; the active index is retained.
evidence: toggleMode updates mode without changing index; the focused test navigates to index 1, toggles mode, and asserts index 1 remains active.

scene-kit.rationale: The window key handler advances or reverses on the supported presentation keys and toggles mode with P.
evidence: onKey maps ArrowRight, Space, and PageDown to next; ArrowLeft and PageUp to prev; P to toggleMode.

scene-kit.rationale: The handler compares horizontal and vertical travel, but it does not record or reject touch count. There are also no focused assertions for predominantly vertical and multi-touch rejection.
evidence: onTouchStart and onTouchEnd use changedTouches[0] without checking gesture touch count; the inspected contract tests contain no vertical or multi-touch swipe case.

scene-kit.rationale: Progress buttons jump to their numbered step, and section buttons jump to the first step in their era.
evidence: Footer progress buttons call goTo(i); Toc buttons call goTo(activeIndex); goTo updates the clamped active index.

scene-kit.rationale: Active progress and section controls expose semantic current state and stable active data hooks.
evidence: Footer assigns aria-current='step' and data-presentation-active to the active progress button; Toc assigns aria-current='location' and the same active hook to the active era.

scene-kit.rationale: Presentation navigation returns for focused buttons and links on their supported keyboard interaction keys, leaving those controls to handle their own events.
evidence: onKey skips button and link targets except P; the focused test sends ArrowLeft to a focused Next button and asserts no presentation navigation occurs.

scene-kit.rationale: Backward navigation clamps the active index to zero.
evidence: goTo applies Math.max(0, ...); the focused test sends ArrowLeft at the first step and asserts data-step-index remains 0.

scene-kit.rationale: Forward navigation clamps the active index to the last step.
evidence: goTo caps the index at count - 1; the focused test sends ArrowRight at the last step and asserts data-step-index remains 1.

scene-kit.rationale: Fit computes one scale from available stage width and height, and Stage uses that same factor for both the viewport dimensions and canvas transform.
evidence: useFitScale subtracts stage top, bottom, and side space, then takes the smaller width and height ratio; Stage applies scale to both dimensions and uses transform: scale(scale).

scene-kit.rationale: The rendered stage consumes the approved 880×380 authored dimensions as its defaults.
evidence: DESIGN_W and DESIGN_H are 880 and 380; Stage uses them for canvas width and height and useFitScale defaults to them.

scene-kit.rationale: The kit emits stable classes and data attributes for presentation, stage, chrome, active controls, and nodes so presentation CSS can target them.
evidence: Presentation and Stage emit data-presentation hooks; Footer and Toc expose hooks and active state; node primitives expose data-presentation-node; sample CSS targets these selectors.

scene-kit.rationale: The kit supplies geometry and behavior while its node primitives and chrome do not impose a palette, typography, borders, or card treatments. The sample presentation supplies those treatments.
evidence: Node primitives forward caller styles without visual defaults; Presentation, Stage, Header, Footer, and Toc use inline positioning; sample style.css defines colors, typography, backgrounds, borders, …

scene-kit.rationale: The delivered presentation uses plain CSS and the kit consumes style and class hooks without requiring a styling framework.
evidence: Talk imports presentation-local style.css; node primitives accept className and style; neither the app nor bootstrap package declares a CSS framework dependency.

scene-kit.rationale: SceneLayer supplies a positioned canvas layer, and node primitives accept precise inline coordinates; the sample uses those mechanisms to place a multi-entity diagram.
evidence: SceneLayer sets absolute inset geometry; Scene's place helper supplies absolute left, top, and width to Boxes, Arrows, and other nodes.

scene-kit.rationale: The kit renders the default link, but its bottom-right placement is supplied by presentation-owned CSS rather than the kit. The kit itself positions only the footer.
evidence: Footer renders the default made by and-scene link without positioning; sample style.css places .presentation-attribution in the footer grid's right column.

scene-kit.rationale: The default attribution exposes stable class and data selectors for host styling.
evidence: Footer renders className='presentation-attribution' and data-presentation-attribution on the link; sample CSS targets the class.

scene-kit.rationale: The header renders no default brand content, while the Presentation brand prop lets the host explicitly supply it.
evidence: Presentation passes optional brand to Header; Header renders only that prop in the brand slot; the focused test checks that no default brand hook is rendered.

presentation-skill.rationale: The skill explicitly requires one concise question at a time and limits questions to information missing from the prompt.
evidence: The new-presentation interview specifies one-at-a-time questioning about missing topic, visual direction, and step details.

presentation-skill.rationale: The skill allows a first draft from partial detail when the user chooses to proceed and explicitly removes a completeness gate.
evidence: The interview instruction says to record what is known, make a coherent first draft, and invite iteration.

presentation-skill.rationale: The instruction to request only missing information bypasses interview questions when the prompt already supplies the required details.
evidence: The new-presentation interview restricts questions to information missing from the user's prompt.

presentation-skill.rationale: A focused integration test copies the bootstrap into a newly created target, installs dependencies there, and verifies that the resulting app builds and renders its route.
evidence: The bootstrap test creates a temporary directory, copies the template to a previously absent materialized-app path, runs npm ci in that app, then asserts successful build and verification.

presentation-skill.rationale: The skill instructs reuse of existing anchors, but the scaffold test exercises only a fresh target. There is no focused evidence that an already scaffolded app is detected and retained.
evidence: The policy says to reuse all existing anchors; the integration setup always copies the bootstrap into a new materialized-app target.

presentation-skill.rationale: No focused test constructs a target with only some anchors and verifies that only missing capabilities are added.
evidence: The skill describes partial-anchor handling, while the bootstrap integration test starts from an absent target and copies the complete template.

presentation-skill.rationale: The bootstrap test copies the complete kit, checks that its files match the canonical kit, and rejects several visual defaults. Direct inspection of the copied kit covers the test’s gaps: its buttons have behavior and positioning but no specified border or button treatment, while its nodes expose styling hooks without supplying a visual theme. The host CSS is a reset; the example’s palette and border are confined to presentation-local CSS.
evidence: The “keeps kit source byte-aligned and free of visual defaults” test compares every copied kit file with the canonical kit and checks for colors, fonts, shadows, theme variables, and numeric padding …
Presentation, chrome, and node components specify geometry, navigation, and motion; their button elements and node primitives specify no border or button treatment.
The bootstrap host CSS contains only box sizing, page sizing, margin reset, and inherited button/link font. The example’s palette and card border are in its own style.css.

presentation-skill.rationale: The bootstrap test resolves the template from the test file's repository location, copies it to a separate app target, installs dependencies in that target, and invokes app scripts from outside the template directory.
evidence: The test derives the template path from import.meta.dirname, calls cp(template, app), runs npm ci with app as cwd, and runs build and verify with --prefix app from scratch.

presentation-skill.rationale: The skill names presentations/ as the monorepo target, but no focused test creates a monorepo, verifies placement there, or checks that root files and unrelated packages survive.
evidence: The monorepo rule appears in the skill; the bootstrap integration test creates only a standalone temporary app.

presentation-skill.rationale: The focused bootstrap test materializes a standalone app at its target path, installs dependencies in that app, and verifies its build and registered route.
evidence: The test copies the complete template into materialized-app, runs npm ci there, and asserts successful lint, build, and verify commands.

presentation-skill.rationale: The skill requires confirmation before writing to a nonempty unscaffolded project, but there is no focused test or workflow evidence showing that this target state pauses before mutation and proceeds after a choice.
evidence: The confirmation instruction is explicit; the bootstrap integration setup uses a new target and has no nonempty-project choice or assertions.

presentation-skill.rationale: The skill directs creation of a presentation folder and one registry entry; the bootstrap router consumes that registry to resolve a slug to a lazily loaded presentation component.
evidence: The policy requires one explicit registry entry, presentations.ts contains an entry with a slug and load function, and Router.tsx maps registered slugs to route components.

presentation-skill.rationale: Although the starter imports CSS from its presentation folder, its visual rules use shared .presentation and chrome selectors. Those global selectors can style other presentations, so the styling is not confined to its owner.
evidence: The starter Talk imports style.css, whose palette and typography rules target .presentation; the bootstrap example stylesheet also targets .presentation and shared chrome selectors.

presentation-skill.rationale: The skill requires preservation and the registry supports separate routes, but the provided presentation styles use global selectors that can alter another presentation's appearance when loaded.
evidence: Both the starter and example stylesheets assign visual values through .presentation; the starter Talk imports that stylesheet without a presentation-specific scope.

presentation-skill.rationale: The skill explicitly requires identifying a unique registered presentation before editing and asking the user to choose when the target is ambiguous.
evidence: The modification instruction says to list registered presentations and ask which one if the request does not name a unique target.

presentation-skill.rationale: SKILL.md limits edits to the selected presentation, but the supplied styling mechanism does not confine those edits’ effects. A presentation imports CSS with global `.presentation` and shared chrome selectors. Every route renders the same kit class names, so editing those rules for one presentation can restyle another after the stylesheet loads.
evidence: The modification policy says to edit only the selected presentation and the smallest necessary registry or host styling files.

Both the authoring style template and delivered presentation CSS use unqualified shared selectors such as `.presentation` and `.presentation-footer`; Talk imports that CSS, and the shared Presentatio…

evidence: The build-and-inspect section mandates npm run build, browser rendering without runtime or console errors, first/last/key screenshots, and npm run verify when present.

presentation-skill.rationale: The skill explicitly forbids reporting success while build, render, or visual-composition problems remain and requires checks to be repeated after fixes.

evidence: The registry and ordered title/caption checks call fail(); the catch handler sets process.exitCode = 1. The missing-title test removes a canonical title and asserts a nonzero status and the sample-ou…

evidence: Each verifier derives its readiness and page URLs from a base using host 127.0.0.1 and passes that host to Vite preview.

evidence: Both readiness loops break immediately on a successful fetch and check server.exitCode only after the fetch attempt and delay.

verification-tooling.rationale: Console errors have a focused propagation test, but no focused executable test injects a page error and verifies its failing step.

verification-tooling.rationale: A step that fails to advance produces a nonzero verification result naming the failing step.

verification-tooling.rationale: A separate project-local inspection command starts a preview and writes screenshots under the project’s artifacts directory.
evidence: The inspect npm script invokes scripts/inspect-presentation.mjs, whose capture loop calls page.screenshot with project-local output paths.

verification-tooling.rationale: The test proves that nine PNG files are written, but does not verify that each file depicts its intended step or that the preview responder is the spawned process.
evidence: The helper clicks a progress item when needed, then screenshots without confirming data-step-index. The integration test asserts only the PNG count, while readiness can accept a stale responder.

verification-tooling.rationale: Capture uses a fixed 900 ms delay without observing animation completion or consuming a transition contract used by persistent scene motion.
evidence: The helper waits 900 ms before each screenshot. Runtime scene nodes use Motion layout animation, and the helper neither observes those animations nor reads their transition settings.

evidence: diagnosePresentation contains missing and default-style branches. The unit test supplies a 9 px link, and the browser test also forces 9 px, so neither isolates the other required warning conditions.

scene-kit.rationale: The step type binds a scene component to its payload type, and the rendered scene uses the supplied payload.
evidence: types.ts defines Step<TPayload> with Scene: SceneComponent<TPayload> and payload: TPayload.
Stage.tsx renders <Scene payload={step.payload} />; steps/Scene.tsx reads payload.beat.

scene-kit.rationale: Stable node IDs provide an implemented layout animation path across grouped step updates.
evidence: nodes/primitives.tsx renders motion nodes with layout and layoutId={id}.
Stage.tsx places the scene in a LayoutGroup; steps/Scene.tsx reuses entity IDs across beats.

scene-kit.rationale: Continuing layout motion does not consume the newcomer delay or a shared settlement signal, and the sample adds nodes without the entry wrapper.
evidence: nodes/primitives.tsx sets layout and layoutId without a transition tied to LAYOUT_T; Appear uses ENTER_DELAY.
steps/Scene.tsx conditionally adds ordinary node primitives as beat increases and does not use Appear.

scene-kit.rationale: The supplied entity path has no mechanism to retain an ordinarily removed child for exit animation.
evidence: Stage.tsx places AnimatePresence around the keyed scene div, not the individual conditional entities.
steps/Scene.tsx conditionally renders entities; nodes/primitives.tsx gives those entities no exit behavior.

scene-kit.rationale: Grouped steps keep a stable scene key, and a focused test checks that the same scene element displays updated content.
evidence: Stage.tsx derives sceneKey from groupKey and Scene identity; steps/index.tsx uses the same groupKey and Scene for every step.
tests/presentation-kit.test.tsx asserts the scene element remains identical after navigation and displays 'B'.

scene-kit.rationale: The explicit grouped update path retains the scene and continuing child branches without replaying entry state.
evidence: Stage.tsx keeps the same keyed scene across grouped steps.
steps/Scene.tsx always renders the 'you' node and retains earlier conditional branches at later beats; nodes/primitives.tsx specifies no initial newcomer animation.

scene-kit.rationale: The sample composes one evolving, positioned scene across its grouped beats.
evidence: steps/index.tsx assigns every step the same Scene and groupKey.
steps/Scene.tsx uses beat conditions and explicit coordinates to accumulate entities in SceneLayer.

scene-kit.rationale: Present mode displays the active title and stage while omitting browse reading chrome.
evidence: Presentation.tsx renders the present title in present mode and renders Toc and Footer only in browse mode.
tests/presentation-kit.test.tsx switches to present mode and asserts the caption is absent.

scene-kit.rationale: Browse mode supplies the specified active-step reading elements, and the table of contents is displayed at wide widths.
evidence: Presentation.tsx renders Toc and Footer in browse mode; Footer.tsx renders title, caption, progress buttons, and previous/next controls.
style.css displays the Toc normally and hides it only at the max-width: 600px breakpoint.

scene-kit.rationale: Mode toggling leaves the active index unchanged, as a focused test verifies.
evidence: usePresentationNav.ts updates only mode in toggleMode.
tests/presentation-kit.test.tsx navigates to index 1, toggles mode, and asserts index 1 remains active.

scene-kit.rationale: The key handler implements forward, backward, and mode-toggle shortcuts.
evidence: usePresentationNav.ts maps ArrowRight, Space, and PageDown to next; ArrowLeft and PageUp to prev; and P to toggleMode.

scene-kit.rationale: The handler compares horizontal and vertical travel but does not reject multi-touch gestures, and the supplied focused tests omit both required rejection cases.
evidence: usePresentationNav.ts stores x and y from changedTouches[0] without recording or checking touch count.
tests/presentation-kit.test.tsx has no predominantly vertical or multi-touch swipe assertions.

scene-kit.rationale: Progress and section buttons call the clamped direct-navigation function.
evidence: Footer.tsx progress buttons call goTo(i); Toc.tsx section buttons call goTo(activeIndex).
usePresentationNav.ts implements goTo with bounds clamping.

scene-kit.rationale: Active progress and section controls expose semantic current-state attributes and stable active hooks.
evidence: Footer.tsx uses aria-current='step' and data-presentation-active for progress.
Toc.tsx uses aria-current='location' and data-presentation-active for sections.

scene-kit.rationale: The global navigation handler leaves focused controls' interaction keys alone, and a focused test checks this behavior.
evidence: usePresentationNav.ts returns for key events targeted at buttons and links, except the mode shortcut P.
tests/presentation-kit.test.tsx sends ArrowLeft to a focused Next button and asserts no step navigation.

scene-kit.rationale: Backward navigation clamps to index zero, with a focused boundary assertion.
evidence: usePresentationNav.ts clamps goTo with Math.max(0, ...).
tests/presentation-kit.test.tsx sends ArrowLeft at the first step and asserts index 0.

scene-kit.rationale: Forward navigation clamps to the last index, with a focused boundary assertion.
evidence: usePresentationNav.ts caps goTo at count - 1.
tests/presentation-kit.test.tsx sends ArrowRight at the last step and asserts index 1.

scene-kit.rationale: The fit calculation accounts for the stage's vertical space and uses one factor for both canvas axes.
evidence: useFitScale.ts subtracts STAGE_LAYOUT top, bottom, and side space and chooses the smaller dimension ratio.
Stage.tsx uses the same scale for viewport width and height and for transform: scale(scale).

scene-kit.rationale: The rendered stage consumes the approved 880×380 defaults.
evidence: constants.ts defines DESIGN_W = 880 and DESIGN_H = 380.
Stage.tsx uses those constants for canvas dimensions; useFitScale.ts uses them as its default design dimensions.

scene-kit.rationale: The kit emits stable selectors for presentation structure, controls, active state, and nodes.
evidence: Presentation.tsx, Stage.tsx, Footer.tsx, Toc.tsx, and nodes/primitives.tsx emit presentation classes or data attributes.
style.css targets those selectors.

scene-kit.rationale: The kit supplies structure and positioning without imposing the sample's palette, typography, borders, or card treatments.
evidence: nodes/primitives.tsx forwards caller styles without visual defaults; kit chrome uses inline placement.
style.css supplies colors, fonts, backgrounds, borders, and card treatments.

scene-kit.rationale: The supplied presentation styles the kit with plain CSS and has no styling-framework dependency.
evidence: Talk.tsx imports style.css; nodes/primitives.tsx accepts className and style.
Both supplied package.json files list no CSS framework.

scene-kit.rationale: The kit supports precise placement, and the sample uses it for a multi-entity diagram.
evidence: nodes/primitives.tsx provides an absolute SceneLayer and forwards node styles.
steps/Scene.tsx places boxes, arrows, and other entities with absolute left and top coordinates.

scene-kit.rationale: The kit renders the default link but does not itself place that link at bottom-right; the sample stylesheet supplies that placement.
evidence: Footer.tsx positions the footer but gives the attribution link no positioning style.
style.css places .presentation-attribution in the footer grid's right column.

scene-kit.rationale: The default attribution has stable selectors that host CSS can target.
evidence: Footer.tsx gives the link className='presentation-attribution' and data-presentation-attribution.
style.css targets .presentation-attribution.

scene-kit.rationale: The header has no default brand content, and the host can supply branding explicitly.
evidence: Presentation.tsx accepts and passes an optional brand prop; Header.tsx renders that prop in the brand slot.
tests/presentation-kit.test.tsx checks that the default render has no brand hook.

presentation-skill.rationale: The normative instruction explicitly requires one concise question at a time about details missing from the prompt.
evidence: skills/presentation/SKILL.md, section 1: “Ask one concise question at a time, requesting only information that is missing from the user's prompt.”

presentation-skill.rationale: The skill explicitly permits a first draft when the user chooses to proceed with incomplete details.
evidence: skills/presentation/SKILL.md, section 1: “if they choose to proceed with partial detail, record what is known and make a coherent first draft without imposing a completeness gate.”

presentation-skill.rationale: A complete prompt leaves no missing information to ask for under the skill's explicit rule.
evidence: skills/presentation/SKILL.md, section 1 restricts questions to information missing from the user's prompt.

presentation-skill.rationale: The focused test creates a new target, copies the bootstrap into it, installs dependencies there, and checks the app's files and build.
evidence: tests/presentation-bootstrap.integration.test.tsx creates scratch with mkdtemp, copies the template to materialized-app, and runs npm ci with app as cwd.
The test checks anchor files, required dependencies, and successful build and verify commands.

presentation-skill.rationale: The supplied focused scaffold test only constructs a fresh target; it does not exercise detection and retention of an already scaffolded app, as the review guidance requires.
evidence: skills/presentation/SKILL.md, section 2 instructs reuse when all anchors exist.
tests/presentation-bootstrap.integration.test.tsx always copies the full bootstrap into a newly named materialized-app target.

presentation-skill.rationale: The supplied focused test never constructs a target with only some anchors or checks that only missing capabilities are added.
evidence: skills/presentation/SKILL.md, section 2 instructs filling missing capabilities in a partial scaffold.
tests/presentation-bootstrap.integration.test.tsx starts from a fresh target and copies the complete bootstrap.

presentation-skill.rationale: The supplied kit components define behavior and geometry without visual defaults. The host CSS is a reset, while palette and card styling live in presentation CSS. A focused executable test copies the bootstrap into a temporary app, compares every copied kit file with the canonical kit, and checks for several visual defaults.
evidence: tests/presentation-bootstrap.integration.test.tsx materializes the bootstrap in a temporary app and tests kit file equality and absence of color, font, shadow, theme-variable, and numeric padding or …

skills/presentation/templates/bootstrap/src/presentation-kit/Presentation.tsx and the supplied chrome and node components use positioning, behavior, and styling hooks without specifying a palette or …
skills/presentation/templates/bootstrap/src/style.css contains reset rules; skills/presentation/templates/bootstrap/src/presentations/example/style.css contains the example palette and card border.

presentation-skill.rationale: The skill defines resolution relative to its own directory, and the focused test resolves the bootstrap independently of the command working directory, copies it to the app target, and installs there.
evidence: skills/presentation/SKILL.md, section 2 says template paths are relative to the skill directory.
tests/presentation-bootstrap.integration.test.tsx derives the template path from import.meta.dirname, copies it to app, runs npm ci with app as cwd, and invokes app scripts from scratch.

presentation-skill.rationale: The supplied focused test never creates a monorepo or checks placement in presentations/ and preservation of root files or unrelated packages.
evidence: skills/presentation/SKILL.md, section 2 specifies presentations/ for monorepos.
tests/presentation-bootstrap.integration.test.tsx creates only a standalone materialized-app target.

presentation-skill.rationale: The focused test constructs a standalone app, installs its dependencies in that app, and checks its files and build.
evidence: tests/presentation-bootstrap.integration.test.tsx copies the bootstrap to materialized-app, runs npm ci there, checks required dependencies and anchor files, and asserts build and verify success.

presentation-skill.rationale: The supplied focused test has no nonempty unscaffolded target, confirmation choice, or assertion that writing pauses until a choice is made.
evidence: skills/presentation/SKILL.md, section 2 requires confirmation before writing to a nonempty unscaffolded project.
tests/presentation-bootstrap.integration.test.tsx uses a fresh target and performs the copy without a choice branch.

presentation-skill.rationale: The skill requires a registry entry, and the supplied registry and router show how a registered slug resolves to a presentation component.
evidence: skills/presentation/SKILL.md, section 4 requires exactly one explicit registry entry and a resolving route.
skills/presentation/templates/bootstrap/src/presentations.ts defines a slug and load function; Router.tsx maps registered slugs to lazy components.

presentation-skill.rationale: The starter imports its own CSS, but that CSS applies visual rules through global presentation and chrome selectors, so its styling is not confined to its presentation.
evidence: skills/presentation/templates/presentation/Talk.tsx imports ./style.css.
skills/presentation/templates/presentation/style.css sets color, background, and font on .presentation and styles shared attribution and progress selectors.

presentation-skill.rationale: The supplied starter and example stylesheets both apply visual values through global selectors. Using the starter can therefore change another presentation's appearance, contrary to preservation.
evidence: skills/presentation/templates/presentation/style.css and skills/presentation/templates/bootstrap/src/presentations/example/style.css both set visual properties on .presentation.
The starter Talk.tsx imports its stylesheet, while the skill directs new presentations to start from that template.

presentation-skill.rationale: The normative instruction explicitly requires resolving an ambiguous modification target before editing.
evidence: skills/presentation/SKILL.md, section 1: “If the request does not name a unique target, list the registered presentations and ask which one.”

presentation-skill.rationale: Presentation-owned CSS uses unqualified selectors for the shared presentation and chrome classes. The shared component renders those classes for any presentation, so loading that CSS can apply its visual rules to another presentation. This is an explicit counterexample to confining a selected presentation's styling effects.
evidence: src/presentations/how-to-make-a-presentation/style.css defines global `.presentation`, `.presentation-header`, `.presentation-footer`, and other shared-class rules.
src/presentations/how-to-make-a-presentation/Talk.tsx imports that stylesheet.
src/presentation-kit/Presentation.tsx renders the shared `.presentation` class, while skills/presentation/SKILL.md requires edits to be confined to the selected presentation.

presentation-skill.rationale: The normative completion gate explicitly requires build, browser render, screenshot inspection, and scaffold verification when available.
evidence: skills/presentation/SKILL.md, section 5 requires npm run build, a real-browser render without runtime or console errors, inspection of representative screenshots, and npm run verify when present.

presentation-skill.rationale: The skill explicitly requires repair and repeated checks before reporting success.
evidence: skills/presentation/SKILL.md, section 5 directs the agent to fix accidental collisions, inspect again, and never report success while build, render, or visual-composition problems remain.

verification-tooling.rationale: The verifier has reachable failure branches for a missing canonical route or sample content, and its catch handler sets a nonzero exit code.
evidence: scripts/verify.mjs checks the registry, titles, captions, and grouped states with fail(), then sets process.exitCode = 1 in the catch handler.
tests/presentation-verification.integration.test.ts removes a canonical title and asserts a nonzero status and sample outline failure.

verification-tooling.rationale: Both verifiers consistently use 127.0.0.1 for preview binding, readiness, and browser navigation.
evidence: scripts/verify.mjs and skills/presentation/templates/bootstrap/scripts/verify.mjs set host to 127.0.0.1, pass it to Vite preview, and derive fetch and page URLs from that host.

verification-tooling.rationale: A successful response from a stale server can end readiness before either verifier checks whether its spawned child exited.
evidence: In both verify.mjs files, the readiness loop breaks immediately when fetch(base) succeeds; the server.exitCode check occurs afterward.

verification-tooling.rationale: The supplied focused tests cover console errors but omit the required page-error propagation case.
evidence: scripts/verify.mjs registers console and pageerror listeners.
tests/presentation-verification.integration.test.ts injects console.error and asserts a step 3 failure, but contains no page-error injection and failing-step assertion.

verification-tooling.rationale: A failed step advance produces a nonzero result that identifies the step, and a focused executable test covers it.
evidence: scripts/verify.mjs fails with the step number if data-step-index does not advance.
tests/presentation-verification.integration.test.ts disables advancement and asserts nonzero status and 'step 2 transition failed'.

verification-tooling.rationale: The project provides a separate inspection command that writes screenshots to a project-local artifacts path.
evidence: package.json maps inspect to scripts/inspect-presentation.mjs.
scripts/inspect-presentation.mjs starts preview and writes each page.screenshot to artifacts/inspection/<slug>.

verification-tooling.rationale: The helper can capture without confirming the selected step or ownership of the preview, and the supplied test only checks the screenshot count.
evidence: scripts/inspect-presentation.mjs clicks a progress item when needed, then screenshots without rechecking data-step-index; its readiness loop can accept a stale responder.
tests/presentation-inspection.integration.test.ts asserts nine PNG filenames but does not verify their depicted steps or preview process.

verification-tooling.rationale: Capture waits a fixed time without observing completion or using a transition contract consumed by persistent scene motion.
evidence: scripts/inspect-presentation.mjs waits 900 ms before each screenshot.
src/presentation-kit/nodes/primitives.tsx uses Motion layout nodes; the helper does not observe their animation completion.

verification-tooling.rationale: The detector omits nested label nodes and suppresses unrelated collisions involving a marked subtree, so it does not inspect the required representative cases.
evidence: scripts/inspection-diagnostics.mjs excludes data-presentation-node="label" from its selector and skips a pair whenever either element has an allow-overlap ancestor.
src/presentation-kit/nodes/primitives.tsx defines Label as a rendered node.
tests/inspection-diagnostics.test.ts uses box nodes and asserts a generic overlap warning; it does not trigger nested label overlap.

verification-tooling.rationale: The marker suppresses a collision even when the other element is outside the marked subtree.
evidence: scripts/inspection-diagnostics.mjs skips a pair if either element has an allow-overlap ancestor.
tests/inspection-diagnostics.test.ts places intentional-a in a marked wrapper and overlapping intentional-b outside it, then expects no warning containing 'intentional'.

verification-tooling.rationale: The diagnostic compares rendered active and inactive styles, and a focused test triggers and asserts the warning.
evidence: scripts/inspection-diagnostics.mjs compares computed color, background color, font weight, and outline style.
tests/inspection-diagnostics.test.ts creates active and inactive progress buttons with matching styles and asserts 'active navigation may be visually indistinct'.

verification-tooling.rationale: The supplied tests exercise undersized attribution but omit focused executable cases for missing and independently browser-default styled attribution.
evidence: scripts/inspection-diagnostics.mjs contains missing-attribution and browser-default-style branches.
tests/inspection-diagnostics.test.ts tests a 9 px attribution link; tests/presentation-inspection.integration.test.ts also forces 9 px while applying browser-default-like styling.
